title: Main Clauses and Verb Position
definition: A German main clause is a complete statement that can stand on its own. In a standard main clause, the conjugated verb occupies the second sentence position (V2), even when another element begins the sentence.

rules.title: Subject first: verb second
rules.explanation: The subject is the first element and the conjugated verb is second.

examples.english: I am going to work today.

rules.title: Another element first: verb still second
rules.explanation: When time, place, or another element is first, the subject usually moves after the verb.

examples.english: Today I am going to work.
In Germany I am learning German.

rules.title: Conjunctions und, aber, oder, denn
rules.explanation: These coordinating conjunctions do not change the normal verb-second order in the clause that follows.

examples.german: Ich lerne Deutsch und mein Bruder lernt Englisch.
examples.english: I learn German and my brother learns English.

examples.german: Ich bin müde, aber ich gehe zur Arbeit.
examples.english: I am tired, but I am going to work.

examples.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.
examples.english: I am staying at home because I am ill.

rules.title: Verb brackets with modal verbs
rules.explanation: With a modal verb, the modal is conjugated in position two and the main verb in the infinitive goes to the end.

examples.english: In the evening I have to work.

rules.title: Verb brackets with separable verbs
rules.explanation: In a main clause, the conjugated verb part comes in position two and the separable prefix goes to the end.

examples.german: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
examples.english: I get up at seven o'clock.

examples.german: Der Zug kommt um acht Uhr an.
examples.english: The train arrives at eight o'clock.

V2.description: The conjugated verb is the second sentence element.

common_mistakes.explanation: The conjugated verb must be in position two.

common_mistakes.correct: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
common_mistakes.explanation: A separable prefix goes to the end in a main clause.

mastery_goal: You can apply the verb-second rule when the subject is first or when time/place comes first, and recognize basic verb brackets.
